answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by giving every identity a living pulse: a signed heartbeat emitted at irregular intervals, bound to one hardware-backed key and to a slowly earned opal record of completed work. A newcomer starts as a mere fable — an unverified story — and only a steady pulse of real, peer-checked jobs over weeks turns it into an opal with weight. Spawning a thousand clones means keeping a thousand convincing heartbeats alive, each with its own work history; the cost of faking the pulse exceeds any gain from the copies.
